sections.html:
Wichita is the largest city in Kansas and the seat of Sedgwick County. The 2020 count was 397,532 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 400,987 across about 166.5 square miles. Every house in the city is valued by the same county office and billed by the same treasurer, whether it sits in Old Town, Delano or a newer subdivision.

The Sedgwick County Appraiser sets the value, and the Sedgwick County Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Wichita does not run its own tax office.

Statements go out each November. The first half or the full amount is due by December 20, and the second half is due May 10 of the next year.

  • Credit cards are accepted online, by phone at 1-833-303-6683, and at the Ruffin Building, 100 N. Broadway, Suite 100.
  • Partial payments are allowed, unless the parcel has been chosen for a tax foreclosure sale.
  • Owners can apply in writing to prepay in monthly amounts, with a $20 minimum for 10 months. The Treasurer decides each application.
  • The only official relief program for seniors or low-income owners is the state Homestead program, reached at 1-785-368-8222.

You can also sign up for a payment reminder from the Treasurer. If you are closing in the fall, ask the title company whether the November bill has posted yet, because it changes the payoff.

sections.h2: How a Wichita tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
Take the appraised value, multiply by 11.5% for a house, then multiply by the combined mill levy. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. For a typical Wichita taxpayer in fiscal year 2025, the county's levy breakdown looks like this:

Taxing bodyMillsShare of bill
USD 259 (Wichita schools)51.38744.9%
City of Wichita32.81628.7%
Sedgwick County28.70125.1%
State of Kansas1.5001.3%

The city's own Mill Levy Facts sheet estimates 32.340 mills for the 2026 budget year, split between the general fund (25.505) and debt service (6.835). The same sheet lists other assessment rates: 25% for commercial property and 12% for vacant lots.

The school share is the largest piece. When a buyer asks what the taxes will be, the answer depends on the school district and any special assessments, so a quick look at the parcel record beats a guess.

Specials are extra assessments for nearby improvements such as streets, sewers and sidewalks. They are normally added to the real property tax bill for 10 to 15 years unless the owner prepaid them.

When you sell, the remaining balance is part of the payoff picture. A house on a recently improved street may carry a special that adds a noticeable amount to every half-year bill. Ask for the specials line on your statement before you set a price or compare offers.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Wichita valuation
sections.html:
You have one appeal per tax year, and the informal route comes first.

  1. Valuation notices are mailed March 1.
  2. Return the appeal form on the back of the notice within 30 days, which is typically March 31.
  3. You get a notice of the interview, usually about 10 days ahead, and meet the appraiser by phone or in person.
  4. A decision letter reports whether the value changed.
  5. If you disagree, appeal to the Board of Tax Appeals small claims division within 30 days of the mailed result. That route is open for single-family homes and for property valued under $3 million that is not agricultural. Filing fees may apply.

If you miss the March window, a Payment Under Protest is the second chance. The form goes in with your December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 if a mortgage company pays the tax. Good evidence includes comparable sales, a recent private appraisal, a purchase contract, dated photos, and signed repair estimates. Send documents at least three business days before your appointment.

Hail and straight-line wind are the repeat problems in Wichita, and roofs take the first hit. If you own a house with storm damage you have not fixed, you have a few choices: file an insurance claim and repair before listing, list it with a repair credit or a lower price, or sell it as-is to a buyer who prices the repairs in.

The county appraiser also accepts signed repair estimates and dated photos of damage as evidence in a value appeal, which can lower the number your tax bill rests on.

sections.h2: What happens if Wichita property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Interest starts after the due dates, and a long delinquency can end in a county auction. The Treasurer lists the real property interest rate as 13% for 2026. It is set from the state rate in K.S.A. 79-2968 plus five percentage points.

Counties must foreclose and sell property with delinquent tax liens under K.S.A. 79-2801. Sedgwick County picks parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years behind. Once the case is filed in District Court, redemption takes cash or certified funds for every delinquent year, plus interest and fees. Buyers at the auction are not responsible for the old taxes, and the owner loses all claim to the property.

Properties with 3 1/2 years of delinquency are eligible for sale, and there is usually one sale a year. Case information for the next auction is posted on the Treasurer's tax foreclosure page. To get a balance, call (316) 660-9000.

sections.h2: Selling a Wichita house that owes back taxes
sections.html:
It can be done. A sale closes through a title company, and delinquent tax is paid from the proceeds like any other lien. What matters is the order of events: if the parcel is already in a foreclosure case, the full balance has to be paid in certified funds to pull it out, so the sale needs a firm closing date.

Steps that usually help:

  • Look up the parcel and note the unpaid years, interest and specials.
  • Check whether your parcel is on the Treasurer's delinquent list or foreclosure list.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff that runs to your expected closing date.
  • Decide whether a value appeal is worth the time before closing.

Cash Home Buyers can look at an as-is Wichita house with tax due and give you a written offer to compare.

sections.h2: What to have ready before closing
sections.html: Bring your latest tax statement, the valuation notice, any specials schedule and a photo ID. If a mortgage is open, request the payoff figure from your lender. The title company will prorate the current year's bill between you and the buyer and pay any back balance from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Wichita property tax paid to the city or the county?
faqs.a: The county collects it. The Sedgwick County Treasurer bills one statement that includes Sedgwick County, the City of Wichita, USD 259 and the state, and the Appraiser sets the value that statement is based on.

faqs.q: What is the Wichita residential assessment rate?
faqs.a: It is 11.5% of appraised value for a house. The assessed value is then multiplied by the combined mill levy.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Wichita valuation?
faqs.a: Return the informal appeal form within 30 days of the notice mailing date, which is typically March 31. After that, a Payment Under Protest can be filed with the December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 when a mortgage company pays.

faqs.q: How long can taxes go unpaid before Sedgwick County sells a house?
faqs.a: Parcels with delinquent taxes of 3 1/2 years are eligible for sale at auction, and the county's warning notice names properties two and a half or three and a half years behind. Once a case is filed, the owner must pay every delinquent year in cash or certified funds.

faqs.q: Does a special assessment affect what I net when I sell?
faqs.a: It can. Specials for streets, sewers or sidewalks are normally added to the tax bill for 10 to 15 years unless prepaid, so check the remaining balance before you compare offers.
